section.title: Introduction
section.para: The Java SE platform has included a small, dependency-free HTTP server implementation, com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer, since Java 21, with support for virtual threads and other improvements in more recent releases. This makes it an attractive option for exposing simple HTTP endpoints, such as REST APIs, health checks, and small web applications, without requiring a Servlet container or any additional third-party dependency.

The JDK HttpServer Whiteboard Specification defines a Whiteboard Pattern, see , for com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpHandler, com.sun.net.httpserver.Filter, and com.sun.net.httpserver.Authenticator objects, as well as for serving static bundle resources. Bundles register these objects as ordinary services with a small number of service properties, and a JDK HttpServer Whiteboard implementation deploys them to an underlying HttpServer.

This specification deliberately defines a small API surface. It does not attempt to provide the full range of features defined by the , such as servlet listeners, error pages, multipart upload handling, or pluggable Servlet Context Helpers. Bundle developers who require the full feature set of the Servlet API should use the Servlet Whiteboard instead. This specification aims to be simple to use for common use cases while relying entirely on classes already present in the Java SE platform.

section.title: Entities
section.para: This specification defines the following entities:

listitem.para: HttpHandler service - A com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpHandler registered as a service to process requests for a given context path.
Filter service - A com.sun.net.httpserver.Filter registered as a service to pre- or post-process requests for one or more matching context paths.
Authenticator service - A com.sun.net.httpserver.Authenticator registered as a service to guard one or more matching context paths.

Resource registration - Any service registered with the resource pattern and prefix properties defined by this specification, causing the whiteboard to serve entries of the registering bundle at one or more context paths. The service object itself is not used.
JDK HttpServer Whiteboard implementation - An implementation that processes the services described above and deploys them to an underlying HttpServer.
JdkHttpServerRuntime service - A service providing runtime introspection into the JDK HttpServer Whiteboard implementation.

section.title: Registering Handlers
section.para: A bundle registers a com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpHandler service to have it deployed at a specific context path. The context path is declared with the service property, which is required for the handler to be picked up by the whiteboard.

table.title: Service properties for HttpHandler Whiteboard services.

entry.para: The context path at which the handler is deployed. Must start with /. See .
A human-readable name for the context. See .
An LDAP filter expression used to target a specific service. See .

section.para: A context path must be unique among the active handler and resource registrations of a JDK HttpServer Whiteboard implementation. If more than one HttpHandler service is registered with the same context path, the service that is first in ranking order, as specified by ServiceReference.compareTo, is deployed. The other services registered for that context path are not deployed and are reflected in the failure DTOs, see , with the failure reason .

When the deployed handler for a context path is unregistered, the JDK HttpServer Whiteboard implementation must deploy the next handler in ranking order that is registered for that context path, if any. This ensures a predictable end result regardless of the order in which handlers are registered or unregistered.
A handler service without a valid osgi.http.jdk.context.path property is not deployed and is reflected in the failure DTOs with the failure reason .

section.title: Registering Filters
section.para: A bundle registers a com.sun.net.httpserver.Filter service to have it applied to one or more context paths. The context path patterns are declared with the service property, which is required.

table.title: Service properties for Filter Whiteboard services.

An LDAP filter expression used to target a specific service. See .

section.para: A filter is applied to a context if at least one of its patterns matches the context path of that handler or resource registration, as defined in . More than one filter can apply to the same context. Filters must be invoked in order of decreasing service ranking; filters with an equal ranking must be invoked in order of ascending service.id.

section.title: Pattern Matching
section.para: Filter and Authenticator patterns, as well as resource patterns, use the following matching rules:

listitem.para: A pattern consisting of only * matches every context path.
A pattern ending with /* matches the string preceding the /* as well as any context path having that string as a proper path prefix. For example, /api/* matches /api and /api/users.
All other patterns must match a context path exactly.

section.title: Registering Authenticators
section.para: A bundle registers a com.sun.net.httpserver.Authenticator service to have it applied to one or more context paths. The context path patterns are declared with the service property, which is required.

table.title: Service properties for Authenticator Whiteboard services.

entry.para: Context path pattern(s) to which this authenticator applies. See . See .
An LDAP filter expression used to target a specific service. See .

section.para: Unlike filters, at most one authenticator can be active for a given context. If more than one registered Authenticator matches a context path, the JDK HttpServer Whiteboard implementation must select the one with the highest service ranking; if more than one has an equal ranking, the one with the lowest service.id must be selected.

section.title: Registering Resources
section.para: A bundle can make its own entries available as static resources by registering any service with the and service properties. The object registered as the service is not used by the JDK HttpServer Whiteboard implementation; only the service properties and the registering bundle are significant. This allows a resource registration to be combined with, for example, an unrelated marker service or a Condition service.

entry.para: Context path pattern(s) at which the resources are served. See . See .
The bundle entry prefix from which resources are served. Must not end with /, except for "/" which denotes the root of the bundle. See .
An LDAP filter expression used to target a specific service. See .

section.para: A request path matching a resource pattern is mapped to the bundle entry obtained by concatenating the resource prefix and the request path relative to the matched pattern. If the relative path is empty or /, it must be treated as /index.html. If no matching bundle entry exists, the JDK HttpServer Whiteboard implementation must respond with HTTP status 404 (Not Found).

Resource patterns share the context path namespace with handler context paths. Unlike handler registrations, resource registrations do not use ranking-based shadowing: the first resource registration successfully activated for a given pattern is used, and any subsequently registered handler or resource registration for the same or an overlapping pattern fails with the reason . Unregistering the active resource registration for a pattern makes that pattern available again for a subsequent registration, but does not retroactively activate a currently failed registration.

section.title: The JdkHttpServerRuntime Service
section.para: The service represents the runtime state of a JDK HttpServer Whiteboard implementation. Each JDK HttpServer Whiteboard implementation registers exactly one JdkHttpServerRuntime service, which can be used to target Whiteboard services defined in this specification to a specific JDK HttpServer Whiteboard implementation using the osgi.http.jdk.target service property.
The JdkHttpServerRuntime service must be registered with the service property.

table.title: Service properties for the JdkHttpServerRuntime service.

entry.para: The endpoint(s) on which the JDK HttpServer Whiteboard implementation is listening, for example http://192.168.1.10:8080/. See .

section.para: The runtime state is provided through Data Transfer Objects (DTOs). The architecture of OSGi DTOs is described in .

The method returns a describing all currently active handler, filter, authenticator, and resource registrations, as well as any registrations that failed. See for more information about the failure DTOs.
The method calculates how a request to a given path would be processed. The returned describes:

listitem.para: The handler or the resource registration whose context path or pattern, respectively, is the longest match for the given path. A handler context path and a resource pattern are compared as strings; if both a handler and a resource registration match the given path with an equal length, the handler must be selected. If no handler or resource registration matches, both the handlerDTO and the resourceDTO fields of the result are null.
All of the filters that apply to the matched handler or resource context, in the order they would be invoked. See .
The authenticator, if any, that applies to the matched handler or resource context. See .

section.title: Error Handling
section.para: Handler, filter, authenticator, and resource registrations that have the required service properties set but cannot be used are reflected in the , , , and respectively, available from the . Registrations of the interfaces described in this specification that do not have the required service properties set are ignored and are not reflected in the failure DTOs.

Each failure DTO extends its corresponding active-state DTO and adds a failureReason field. The class defines the possible values, reusing the numeric values of the identically named constants defined by the org.osgi.service.servlet.runtime.dto.DTOConstants class of the Servlet Whiteboard Specification, so that the same failure reason has the same meaning across whiteboard specifications.

entry.para: The service is shadowed by another service, for example another service with the same context path or an overlapping pattern but a higher service ranking.
An exception occurred while initializing the handler, filter, authenticator, or resource context.
The service is registered in the service registry but getting the service fails as it returns null.
The service properties are invalid, for example a missing or malformed context path or pattern property.

section.title: Security
section.para: This section only applies when executing in an OSGi environment which is enforcing Java permissions.

Bundles that need to register HttpHandler, Filter, Authenticator, or resource Whiteboard services must be granted ServicePermission[interfaceName, REGISTER], where interface name is the name of the service interface used for the registration, or of the marker service interface in case of a resource registration.
The JDK HttpServer Whiteboard implementation must be granted ServicePermission[interfaceName, GET] to retrieve these Whiteboard services from the service registry.
Bundles that need to introspect the runtime state need ServicePermission[org.osgi.service.jdkhttp.runtime.JdkHttpServerRuntime, GET] to obtain the JdkHttpServerRuntime service.

To serve resources registered by other bundles, the JDK HttpServer Whiteboard implementation must be granted AdminPermission[*,RESOURCE], since serving resources requires calling Bundle.getEntry on behalf of the registering bundle, and this method requires the caller to have AdminPermission[bundle,RESOURCE].
